A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TDM research, with matching core methods and experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including v1's checklist and v2's additional appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original TDM experiments on torus distributions, protein/RNA torsion angles, SO(n) mixtures, and quantum time-evolution operators, including likelihood results and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds quantum-generation comparisons with RFM in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Equations (5)-(7) revise the general reverse SDE/ODE to evaluate the score and noise coefficients consistently at gamma(T-t). The TDM training objectives and Algorithms 1-4 remain unchanged; the correction does not alter the reported constant-gamma experiments. Appendix G's expanded architecture description does not establish an architecture change.

E1.justification: Both versions cover checkerboard/Pacman and dimensional-scaling torus data, protein/RNA angles, SO(n) mixtures, quantum oscillators, and transverse-field Ising models. Appendix H remains within the existing quantum-generation tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix H, Figures 10-11, adds RFM as an evaluated comparator for the quantum oscillator and Ising-model experiments, where v1 showed TDM against ground truth. The existing protein/RNA, torus, and SO(3) comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The rightmost quantum-oscillator panel's reported matrix size changes from U(6) in v1 Figure 3 to U(8) in v2 Figure 8. This establishes a revised setting label, not a rerun. NLL evaluation and the 9:1 split remain unchanged; the expanded training settings in Appendix G are newly disclosed details.

E4.justification: The dimensional-scaling analysis is retained as v1 Figure 5/v2 Figure 2. Appendix H adds quantum benchmark comparisons through marginal scatter plots, without a distinct ablation, sensitivity analysis, robustness test, or diagnostic protocol.

E5.justification: v1's checklist explicitly identifies the reported variability as standard deviations. v2 removes that checklist without retaining this explanation, although the numerical uncertainty entries remain unchanged. Neither version specifies experimental run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: Figures 10-11 add quantum-generation results comparing RFM, TDM, and ground truth, supporting the reported finding of better boundary-detail fidelity for TDM. Existing quantitative results remain unchanged, including Table 1's TDM RNA NLL of -6.86 ± 0.46 and the SO(3) log likelihood of 0.292 ± 0.07.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.3 adds Assumption 1 and a nonasymptotic Wasserstein convergence/error bound for OSI, attributed to Kong and Tao, with proof details deferred to that work. Equations (5)-(7) correct reverse-time coefficients. Appendix F also changes the flow definition's differentiation variable from t to s, inconsistently with its subsequent use.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain the same scientific claims: trivialized score learning, manifold-preserving integration, strong torus/protein/RNA generation, and generation on higher-dimensional SO(n) and unitary groups. The added conclusion largely summarizes these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 suggests that hardwiring geometry may improve data efficiency and attributes RFM's noisier quantum-distribution boundaries to approximations. Appendix D.3 newly asserts that its bound covers forward and backward integration. The general-manifold limitation remains, while the specific discussion of specialized quantum architectures is condensed.

D1.justification: Appendix G expands a brief architecture reference into explicit embeddings, normalization, skip-connected MLPs, activations, widths, and depth ranges. It adds time-horizon ranges, learning rate, scheduler, batch size, and training limits. v2 also supplies a repository link, whereas v1 only states that code was supplied as supplementary material.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Riemannian Diffusion Mixture and further momentum/SE(3) literature. A substantive but focused FrameDiff discussion acknowledges its fixed-space learning and projection-free simulation, distinguishing TDM through broader Lie-group applicability. Mezzadri's sampling reference is removed; publication updates to retained works do not constitute new citations.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify trivialization, matrix representations, and Abelian factorization. The preliminaries pointer is incorporated into Method, the final section becomes a conclusion with limitations, and the checklist is removed. Most scientific prose and the existing appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds a conceptual method diagram and two substantial three-way quantum-comparison grids. It rearranges and reformats the existing result figures, expands captions, moves Algorithm 1 earlier, and adopts ICLR headings and headers. These collectively substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's sparse implementation description, v2 substantially improves reproducibility information and adds useful RFM quantum comparisons and clearer FrameDiff positioning. The gains are tempered by losing the standard-deviation explanation and introducing theoretical inconsistencies: Appendix D.3 does not establish that its position-only potential setup covers the learned backward sampler, and Appendix F changes the flow-time derivative inconsistently. The retained core quantitative evidence is unchanged.
